speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help determine the cause of the newborn's jaundice, could you please tell me the baby's gestational age at birth and how many hours old they are now? Also, has the baby been feeding well and producing adequate wet diapers?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby been producing adequate wet diapers and stools, and is the stool color pale or clay-colored? Also, has there been any history of maternal blood type incompatibility or recent infections?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the family history of liver failure and current jaundice, I need to rule out biliary atresia. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal ultrasound and family history, I need to check for metabolic causes like galactosemia. REQUEST TEST: Serum Galactose and Urinary Reducing Substances.

speaker: Doctor
text: The family history of a sibling dying from liver failure is highly suspicious for Galactosemia, which can present with normal initial reducing sugar screens if the diet was not fully established or due to assay limitations. REQUEST TEST: Blood Glucose and Liver Function Tests.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood Glucose: Not provided; Liver Function Tests: Bilirubin Total 16.1 mg/dL, Bilirubin Direct 0.7 mg/dL, Alkaline Phosphatase 22 U/L, AST 12 U/L, ALT 12 U/L

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal liver enzymes and direct bilirubin make biliary atresia and severe hepatocellular disease unlikely, pointing toward a conjugation defect. I will request the enzyme assay to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Glucuronosyltransferase Activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: The significantly decreased glucuronosyltransferase activity confirms the diagnosis of Crigler-Najjar syndrome type I. DIAGNOSIS READY: Crigler-Najjar syndrome type I
